subject: Request: WellScope - short-term debug log retention exception & proof-of-delete
messages:
From: Ari Levin <ari.levin@wellscope.health>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: compliance@wellscope.health
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Short-term retention exception for debug logs & proof-of-delete

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We have a couple of follow-ups from our security team around log retention. Our auditors are asking whether WellScope (as a tenant) can request a 30-day retention policy for full request/response debug logs during an initial integration period (we typically need richer logs to validate de-identification).

Specifically they want:
- Confirmation Redwood supports tenant-scoped retention overrides for debug/trace logs.
- A written playbook that describes the process to request an exception, approval path, and how deletion is verified.
- Evidence/artifacts showing a previous delete cycle (proof-of-delete) and a sample redacted log.

Can you share what you can provide? Also please confirm any security controls (KMS/HSM access, access audit logs) applied during this period.

Thanks,
Ari Levin
Director, Security & Compliance
WellScope Health

---
Attachment: none
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: Ari Levin <ari.levin@wellscope.health>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Short-term retention exception for debug logs & proof-of-delete

Hi Ari —

Appreciate the clear ask. Short answers up front: yes, Redwood supports tenant-scoped retention overrides for debug logs; we can implement a 30-day window scoped to the tenant. We also have a documented exception workflow and can provide a proof-of-delete artifact from a previous, similar exception (redacted).

I'll coordinate the playbook and evidence pack and pull Markus in for the technical details on the delete verification. High-level items we'll provide:
- Exception request form and approval flow (security + product sign-off)
- Implementation runbook (how we isolate, enable, and roll back the override)
- Proof-of-delete package (manifest + SHA256 digest + timestamped deletion cert)
- Sample redacted log extract showing PII removal and retention markers
- Controls overview (KMS usage, access logs retention, and audit trail)

Can you confirm the canonical contact for WellScope who will sign the exception (legal or security)? Also, do you need this package in a specific format (SIG/CAIQ mapped artifacts or a plain PDF pack)?

I'll aim to send the first draft of the playbook and the sample artifacts by Monday.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Manager, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: none
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ari Levin <ari.levin@wellscope.health>

Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Short-term retention exception for debug logs & proof-of-delete

Ari / Marissa —

Adding the technical specifics we discussed offline. Summary of the implementation and delete verification approach we will include in the pack:

1) Tenant-scoped override
- We create a short-lived retention profile tied to WellScope tenant ID in our config service. This is strictly applied to the "debug" log stream for the tenant. Host-level logs and core audit trails are unaffected.

2) Isolation and access controls
- Keys: all exported artifacts are encrypted at rest with customer-tenant keys managed in our KMS. Engineering ops uses role-based access; any access during the exception is recorded in our audit log.

3) Deletion & verification
- Deletion job is run once the exception window ends: it performs targeted deletes across primary and s3-backed cold storage, then generates a deletion manifest (file list + object ids) and SHA256 digests.
- We create a signed deletion certificate (signed by our Compliance lead) with timestamps and store a copy in the tenant's evidence folder.
- For external verification, we can provide a redacted sample of the manifest and a corresponding sample log extract with identifying fields masked.

4) Additional mitigations
- Continuous prefix/KV caching is disabled for the tenant during the window to avoid residual copies in memory.
- We can enable a short audit stream export to a WellScope S3 (locked) for independent review during onboarding if you prefer.

Attachments I'm attaching to this email: retention-exception-playbook.pdf (draft), sample-log-redaction.csv (redacted sample), proof-of-delete-20260614.txt (example of signed cert). Note these are redacted demo artifacts. We will prepare a full, exportable SIG/CAIQ mapping file if requested.

Let me know if you want the deletion cert to include additional attestations (e.g., vendor third-party witness).

-Markus
Staff Engineer, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference

Marissa/Markus —

This is great, thanks. Compliance wants the draft playbook and the redacted artifacts in a single signed PDF for our internal reviewers. They'd also like a short statement confirming that while the tenant override is active:

- No other tenants' debug logs are affected
- There are no persistent copies in any caches or monitoring exports beyond the 30-day window

If you can include those explicit bullets in the playbook and send the signed PDF, we can route to our legal to sign the exception. Also, please include the date format you use in the deletion cert (UTC/ISO).

I'll be the primary signer on behalf of WellScope. Legal will loop in if they need to be included.

Thanks,
Ari
